_provenance: The key agent's candidates per step of the twenty-third chain (eval/results/adventureworks_incremental/20261031T032606335763Z-run1.trace.jsonl, the five emit_business_keys calls in order). Copied for WP125's count guard; eval/results is not versioned.

adventureworks_person.rationale: REQ-002 states each business entity is identified by a single company-wide number unique across all parties; REQ-003 uses it as the integration point and REQ-069 assumes it is stable and never re-used (to be confirmed).
REQ-008 and REQ-009 state a person is identified by the company-wide business entity number and has no separate identifier; it is unique, business-recognised and non-null.
REQ-006 describes a globally unique identifier for replication, and REQ-007 says it has no business meaning and is not a business key; it is technical metadata only.

REQ-001-2 states each postal address is identified by its own address number; it is the only identifier the requirements give for an address, although it is system-assigned, so confidence is capped just below the explicit-key range.
REQ-016-2 and REQ-012-2 define a reference list of address types that every party-address relationship must reference; no code is given, so the type ID is the identifier, with Name as an alternative.
REQ-016-2 says each address type has a descriptive name such as Billing, Home or Shipping; the name is recognised by the business, but its uniqueness and stability are not stated.
REQ-039-2 and REQ-038-2 define a contact type reference list used by every contact relationship; the identifier is not explicitly stated, so the type ID is the likely key.
REQ-039-2 says each contact type has a descriptive name; the business recognises it, but uniqueness and stability are not stated.
REQ-040 and REQ-039 define a reference list of phone number types that qualifies each telephone number; no business code is given, so the type ID is the identifier.
REQ-040 gives each phone number type a name such as home, work or mobile. REQ-044 warns that renames affect history, so the name is not stable enough to rank highly.
REQ-022-2 states each country or region is identified by its ISO standard code; it is stable, unique, business-recognised and non-null.
REQ-023-2 states each state or province is identified by its own number, which makes it the explicit identifier. It is system-assigned, so confidence is capped just below the top range.
REQ-023-2 says states carry an ISO standard code, but REQ-026-2 says the country code is substituted where no genuine code exists. That weakens its uniqueness and non-null properties.

REQ-032 says each email address is numbered within the person, and REQ-033 says it belongs to exactly one person and is meaningless without that person. The key is therefore the person's business entity number plus this number (a weak entity).
REQ-031 records email addresses, but the requirements do not say the address text is unique. REQ-036 and REQ-037 also say it changes over time, so it is unstable.

REQ-038, REQ-039 and REQ-042 say a telephone number belongs to exactly one person and is qualified by its type. It is identified in combination with the person's business entity number and the phone number type.
REQ-014-2 explicitly states that the combination of party, address and address type makes a party-address relationship unique; REQ-015-2 confirms the same address may appear under different types.
REQ-041-2 explicitly states that the combination of organisation, person and role makes a contact relationship unique; REQ-042-2 confirms the many-to-many cardinality.

REQ-050 says a credential is attached to a person by the same business entity number and each person has at most one credential. REQ-049 says the credential may be out of scope, so this is conditional.

adventureworks_humanresources.rationale: REQ-002 describes the national identification number as unique and the strongest natural business identifier for a person; REQ-001 requires unique, consistent identification. It is stable and business-recognised, though nullability is not stated.

REQ-003 states each employee is registered under a company-wide business entity number, and REQ-004 needs it to reconcile with the wider business-entity register. It is unique, non-null and stable, but it is a shared register number rather than the HR-specific identity.
REQ-005 says the network login is an IT identifier and must not be treated as the business identity of the person, so it is a weak candidate.
REQ-006 says the technical replication row identifier has no business meaning, so it is a system-generated key and a very weak business key.
REQ-032 says each department is known by its name, and REQ-031 describes a department register. Uniqueness and stability are not explicitly stated, and REQ-036 implies the description can change.
DepartmentID is the source identifier for departments in REQ-031, but the requirements do not mention it as a business identifier. It is likely a system-assigned surrogate, so it scores low.
REQ-038 says each shift is known by its name. REQ-041 warns that definitions can change under the same name, which weakens stability and uniqueness.
ShiftID is the source identifier for the shift register in REQ-037, but the requirements do not call it a business identifier. It is likely a surrogate, so it scores low.

REQ-015-2 states an individual assignment is recognised by the combination of employee, department, shift and start date. REQ-013-2 and REQ-014-2 require repeat assignments to stay separate, which the start date allows.
REQ-016-2, REQ-017-2 and REQ-018-2 describe pay changes per employee on defined effective dates. REQ-019-2 says that date is business-meaningful, so the pair identifies a pay record.

REQ-030-2 requires recording job candidates, and no other identifier for a candidate appears in the requirements. JobCandidateID is probably system-generated, so it is the only available key but a weak one.

adventureworks_production.rationale: REQ-002 explicitly states the product number is unique and is the natural business key used day to day; REQ-001 requires unambiguous identification. Stable, unique, business-recognised.

System-generated surrogate in the operational system; REQ-055-3 says technical identifiers without business meaning should not surface in reporting. Weak business key, though used as FK in other sources.
REQ-004 states the product name is not guaranteed unique and must not be relied on to identify a product.
REQ-030 says a product category must be identifiable by its name (description); REQ-029 defines it as the top level of the hierarchy.
System-generated surrogate; weak business key (REQ-055-3).
REQ-031 says a product subcategory must be identifiable by its name; it belongs to exactly one category (REQ-032).
System-generated surrogate; weak business key (REQ-055-3).
REQ-036 states the business must be able to identify a product model by its name; shared by several products (REQ-037).
System-generated surrogate; weak business key (REQ-055-3).
REQ-044 states each culture is identified by a short culture code; this is a business-recognised, stable code (not a generated number).
REQ-093 states each unit of measure is identified by a short code; stable and business-recognised, used across quantity, size and weight (REQ-094).
REQ-001-2 states each manufacturing location is identified by a name (shop floors and work centres).
System-generated surrogate; weak business key (REQ-055-3).

REQ-019-2 requires each work order to be uniquely identifiable; WorkOrderID is the only listed identifier, and the business raises and refers to work orders (REQ-018-2, REQ-007-3), though it is system-assigned.
REQ-026-2 says scrap reasons are a standard list each carrying a failure description; the name is the business-recognised value, though uniqueness is not explicitly stated.
System-generated surrogate; weak business key (REQ-055-3).

REQ-001-3 requires each inventory transaction to be identified uniquely; TransactionID is the only identifier, though system-generated. The same ID exists in live and archive stores (REQ-018-3, REQ-022-3).
REQ-024-3 requires identifying each review; no natural identifier is stated (reviewer name and e-mail are personal data, REQ-034-3), so the generated ID is the only option.
REQ-057 and REQ-058 describe illustrations without a natural identifier; the generated ID is the only identifying source column.
REQ-043 describes a library of free-text descriptions with no natural key; the generated ID is the only identifier.
REQ-049 describes a photograph library with no natural identifier stated; the generated ID is the only identifier.

REQ-060 requires identifying each document in the controlled library, and REQ-062 requires reconstructing the hierarchy; DocumentNode is the hierarchical position identifier. Title is not stated as unique.
System-generated GUID; weak business key (REQ-055-3).

REQ-068 and REQ-069 say each document carries an engineering change approval number and documents trace to the authorising change; recognised by the business, though the change object is not described further.

adventureworks_purchasing.rationale: REQ-002 explicitly states a vendor is identified in business terms by its vendor account number, used by purchasing staff and in correspondence; it is business-recognised and unique (stable/non-null assumed from the Vendor source column AccountNumber).

REQ-003 requires retaining the internal identifier because other purchasing records (e.g. purchase orders via VendorID, ProductVendor) point to it. It is a system-assigned internal key, so it is a weaker business key than the account number, but it is needed for referential joins.
REQ-032 states a purchase order is identified in business terms by its purchase order number; it is unique, referenced by order lines (REQ-002-2) and used by the business.

adventureworks_purchasing.field: PurchaseOrderID + PurchaseOrderDetailID (purchase order with line number)
adventureworks_purchasing.rationale: REQ-002-2 states a line is identified by the purchase order it belongs to together with its line number; the composite is unique within the line universe and non-null.

REQ-030 requires consistently identifying each purchased product and joining to product information maintained outside purchasing; REQ-003-2 and REQ-017 show ProductID is the product reference on order lines and supply relationships. The requirements do not state a business-assigned product number, so ProductID is the only grounded key.

REQ-017 explicitly states the supply relationship is identified in business terms by the pairing of product and vendor (REQ-015, REQ-016, REQ-027-2); the composite is unique per combination and non-null.
REQ-021-2 states a shipping method is identified in business terms by the shipping company name; it is business-recognised, though name uniqueness and stability are not explicitly guaranteed.

REQ-021-2 also names an internal shipping method identifier used on purchase orders (REQ-037, REQ-030-2). It is used by the business in purchase orders and is stable and unique, but it is internal/system-assigned, so it ranks below the name.
REQ-026-2 states the technical replication identifier has no business meaning and is not required for reporting, so it is a very weak business key.

REQ-034 and REQ-036 indicate only the identity of the creating employee is available in purchasing, and PurchaseOrderHeader carries EmployeeID. Employee details come from the HR area, so this is a reference key and no business-assigned employee number is stated.

adventureworks_sales.rationale: REQ-002 states every customer is identified by the account number assigned by the accounting system, which uniquely identifies the customer; REQ-053-3 says it is taken as given from source (stable, unique, business-recognised).
System-generated surrogate in the Customer source; not named by the requirements as the identifier, so it is a weak business key (only a technical fallback).
REQ-015 states every sales order is identified by its unique sales order number; REQ-053-3 confirms it is taken as given from the source.
System-generated internal identifier in SalesOrderHeader; weak as business key since REQ-015 designates the order number as the identifier.

REQ-045 requires each order line to be identified within its order using one incremental unique number per product sold; it should be combined with the order key (SalesOrderNumber/SalesOrderID) to form a composite key.
REQ-010 states each store is identified by its business entity reference; unique, non-null and used by the business.
REQ-060 states each sales representative is identified by their business entity reference, also their employee reference; stable, unique and non-null.

REQ-068 and REQ-056-2 describe a catalogue of territories, each with a name, but no explicit identifier is stated; TerritoryID is the source's territory identifier and is referenced by customers, orders and representatives (REQ-006, REQ-019, REQ-061).
REQ-068 says each territory has a territory name; it is business-recognised but uniqueness and stability are not stated.

REQ-075 says cards are identified by the card record held in the operational system, so CreditCardID is the identifier the requirements point to, although it is system-generated. The card number is sensitive (REQ-078) and is not preferred as a key.
REQ-076 lists card number as an attribute. It is sensitive payment data (REQ-078, REQ-079, REQ-047-3), and uniqueness is not stated, so it is a poor business key.
REQ-022-2 states currencies are identified by their ISO currency code; stable, unique, non-null and business-recognised.

REQ-024-2 and REQ-059-2 describe a rate by the date it was obtained, the currency converted from and the currency converted to (daily series, REQ-016-3). This is a natural composite key. CurrencyRateID is only a surrogate.
System-generated source identifier for a rate; weak business key. The requirements describe rates by date and currency pair (REQ-024-2).

REQ-051 and REQ-009-2 treat a special offer (promotional code) as a catalogue item, but no explicit identifier is stated; SpecialOfferID is the source identifier referenced from order lines (REQ-047-2). The description is not stated to be unique.
REQ-055 describes a sales reason catalogue with a description and a category but names no identifier; SalesReasonID is the source identifier used to link orders to reasons (REQ-056, REQ-057).

REQ-001-2 and REQ-002-2 state cart items are each identified within their shopping cart, so a composite of cart identifier and item identifier is the natural key. ShoppingCartItemID alone is a surrogate.
REQ-002-2 and REQ-061-2: the shopping cart identifier is known for each cart item and a cart contains one or more items.

REQ-035-2 describes a register of tax rates, and REQ-060-2 says a rate applies to one jurisdiction for a given tax type. No explicit identifier is stated, so SalesTaxRateID is a source identifier used as a fallback. A jurisdiction plus tax type composite is an alternative natural key.

REQ-046 and REQ-046-2 reference the product on order lines, cart items and offers (REQ-001 says product information is maintained outside the sales area). ProductID is the referenced identifier and is needed as a hub anchor.
REQ-004 and REQ-080 reference persons (customers and card holders) maintained outside the sales area (REQ-001); the person is referenced through the business entity ID in PersonCreditCard.
REQ-069 and REQ-032-2 reference countries/regions for territories and currencies. They are maintained outside the sales area (REQ-001) and referenced by CountryRegionCode in the source.
REQ-036-2 says tax rates apply to a state or province, which is maintained outside the sales area (REQ-001); the source references it via StateProvinceID.
REQ-029, REQ-030 and REQ-063-2 reference billing and shipping addresses, maintained outside the sales area (REQ-001); referenced by BillToAddressID/ShipToAddressID.
REQ-031 and REQ-064-2 reference the shipping method, maintained outside the sales area (REQ-001); referenced by ShipMethodID on the order.
